name: Kinetic-Anchored Degenerate Aether Frame (KADAF)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture introduces a degenerate aether vector u_mu that provides the necessary preferred-frame carrier for correct MOND lensing without under-lensing. Crucially, the vector's kinetic normalization is anchored by an independent constant mass scale M_A (independent of the MOND acceleration scale a_0), satisfying the P7 requirement that screening must not kill the kinetic term. The coupling to the metric is explicitly multiplied by e^-y, ensuring that the preferred-frame response is screened in the high-acceleration Solar System limit, while the degenerate kinetic term remains finite and healthy, avoiding the strong-coupling wall that killed the khronometric candidate.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the degenerate aether propagates as a single longitudinal mode with a finite sound speed determined by M_A. The e^-y screening factor suppresses the preferred-frame coupling (alpha_PPN ~ e^-y) in the Solar System, ensuring compliance with PPN constraints. The lensing potential is sourced by the aether frame in a way that breaks the slip-lock theorem (DC-013) because the frame is explicitly present and not diff-invariant, allowing for the correct MOND-enhanced lensing without the f(R)-type slip.
inequivalence_argument: This is inequivalent to DC-002 (AeST) because the kinetic normalization is independent of the screening factor (P7-safe) and the coupling is explicitly e^-y screened, unlike the constant K_B coupling in AeST. It is inequivalent to the khronometric candidate (DC-010) because the kinetic term is not degenerate in the time direction in a way that causes strong coupling as eta->0; instead, the degenerate vector has a fixed finite normalization. It avoids the DC-013 slip-lock because the presence of the explicit preferred frame u_mu breaks the diff-invariance that locks the frame-free theory to the under-lensing ray.
